newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW - Manila's Shell to defend market share.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Manila's Shell to defend market share.

text.p: Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp said on Tuesday its expects to hold on to its market share in the recently deregulated oil market despite burgeoning competition.

"We aim to maintain our market share. Given that the oil industry has deregulated, it's a tall order to even keep our market share," newly-appointed Pilipinas Shell president Oscar Reyes told Reuters in an interview.
Pilipinas Shell, a unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell group of companies, is one of three local oil refiners.
Its market share of 33.7 percent is second to Petron Corp, partly owned by Saudi Arabia's Aramco.

"We are clearly seeing competition barely 75 days after the start of full deregulation. We see new players entering areas where investments are relatively modest and set-up time is easier," said Reyes.

Reyes said competition was noticeable especially in the retail and liquefied petroleum gasoline (lpg) business. About 35 companies have registered with the Department of Energy to invest in marketing and retail facilities.
Competition in the commercial and industrial sector is also evident.
"We clearly aim to service sectors like the National Power Corp which previously was the preserve of Petron," Reyes said.
But new investments are likely to be focused on the non-refining aspect of the oil sector, Reyes said.
"The current refining capacity in the region plus the tariff rates situation do not encourage investments in (refining)."
Reyes said a surplus in refining capacity in the region makes it more economically viable to import petroleum products rather than set up a new refinery.
An existing four percent tariff differential between crude and petroleum products also encourages imports rather than a new domestic refinery, Reyes added.
To beat off competition, Reyes said Shell started upgrading its service stations prior to the start of deregulation in February.
He said the company was the first to increase its refinery capacity now at 155,000 barrels per day (bpd).
"We have invested heavily, over $1 billion in the last five years. We saw deregulation coming and have prepared for it," Reyes added.

This year, the company has earmarked 2.8 billion pesos ($106.46 million) in capital expenditures from 2.5 billion last year. The amount will finance in part upgrading of refinery facilities, the construction of 50 new stations and improvement of 40 others.
Reyes said Shell also plans to implement a reorganisation by May which will entail a reduction in workforce by 10 percent to "a little over" 1,000.
The company recently reported a 48 percent increase in net income to 2.52 billion pesos in 1996 from 1.7 billion.

Asked on projected profits this year, Reyes said: "We will likely be slightly higher than 1996. It's a volatile situation because it will be the first time that we are operating in a deregulated environment." Conversion $=26.30
